summary: Diego Cosmelli earned his PhD at the École Polytechnique, studying under doctoral supervisor Francisco Varela.

Diego Loukota, an expert in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, earned an MA from Peking University and completed his PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles in 2019.

Indologist and linguist Dieter B. Kapp completed his Dr. phil. at Heidelberg University under Hermann Berger in 1971. He worked at Heidelberg, held guest professorships at Munich and Berlin, and was Director of Indology and Tamilistics at Cologne (1990–2006).
Dieter Conrad worked in Indology and law. He earned his Dr.iur. at Heidelberg University in 1963, where he subsequently served as a Senior Research Fellow from 1963 to 1997.

Dieter George, an Indologist and historian, studied at Calcutta and completed his PhD under Wilhelm Rau at Marburg in 1966. He worked at the Royal Library of Berlin (~1972–1985) and served as Geschäftsführer of the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft (1977–1985).

Dieter Gunkel specializes in linguistics and Indology, earning a BA from Middlebury and a PhD from UCLA (2010). He held posts at the University of Munich, the University of Richmond (2017–2024), and UCLA, where he became Associate Professor in 2024.

Indologist Dieter Schlingloff completed his Dr. phil. under Ernst Waldschmidt at Göttingen (1952) and his Habilitation at Berlin (1961). He taught at Göttingen, Kiel (1968–1971), and was Honorary Professor at Munich (1972–1996) and Leipzig (2005).
Dieter Schrapel is an Indologist who earned his doctoral degree at the University of Marburg under the supervision of Wilhelm Rau, attested in 1970.

Tibetologist Dieter Schuh studied at Cologne and Bonn, completing his PhD (1972) and Habilitation (~1972–1976) at Bonn. He served as professor of Tibetology at Bonn (1978–2007) and founded the International Institute for Tibetan and Buddhist Studies, serving as Managing Director (~2006).

Diether Lauenstein studied Indology and religious studies, completing a Dr.theol. under Johannes Nobel at Marburg (1943) and habilitating at Greifswald. He held a post at the University of Greifswald in 1944.

Dietmar Rothermund specialized in South Asian history and Indology, earning his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania (~1959). He served as Chair of the History of South Asia at Heidelberg University from 1968 to 2001.
Dieuke Gaastra was an Indologist who studied at Utrecht University under Johan Hendrik Gallée and doctoral supervisor Willem Caland, completing her PhD in 1906.

Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche was a master in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Shechen Gyaltsap and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö. He succeeded Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje from 1987 to 1991 and taught numerous prominent Buddhist students.

Archaeologist and Indologist Dilip K. Chakrabarti studied at the University of Calcutta (~1961–1965). He taught archaeology at Calcutta (1965–1977) and Delhi (1977–1990) before becoming Professor of South Asian Archaeology at the University of Cambridge (1990–2008).

Dilip Kumar Biswas was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta under Prabodh Chandra Bagchi, later holding academic posts at Visva-Bharati University (~1949) and Calcutta.

Dilli Raman Regmi was an Indologist and historian. He earned an M.Litt from the University of Madras and a D. Litt. from Patna University (~1940–1961), and worked as a teacher at Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith.

Dina Bangdel worked in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She held academic posts at Virginia Commonwealth University (~2002–2017) and Ohio State University (attested 2006).

Dina Johanna Kohlbrugge, a scholar of Indology and Iranian studies, earned her PhD under Jan Gonda at Utrecht University in 1938. She taught at Utrecht, serving as Professor of Iranian language and literature from 1956 to 1981.

Indologist and linguist Dines Andersen completed his PhD at the University of Copenhagen in 1892, having studied under Fausbøll, Thomsen, and Verner. He worked at Copenhagen University Library and was Docent (1901) and Professor (1903–1927) at Copenhagen.

Indologist and historian Dineschandra Sircar served as Government Epigraphist for India at the Archaeological Survey of India. He also taught at the University of Calcutta, where he became Carmichael Professor and Head of Ancient Indian History and Culture in 1962.
